title: What happens when String values are concatenated with +
answer: The `+` operator on Strings is language-level concatenation syntax. Constant-only expressions may be folded by the compiler. For runtime values, modern Java compilers typically emit an `invokedynamic` string-concatenation call site backed by `StringConcatFactory`, allowing the JVM to choose an efficient concatenation strategy; older explanations that say the compiler always rewrites `+` to an explicit `StringBuilder` are no longer universally accurate. In loops or repeated incremental construction, an explicit `StringBuilder` is still often clearer and avoids repeatedly creating concatenation results.
